newsitem.title: USA: Calif. says rice, cotton production seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Calif. says rice, cotton production seen rising.

text.p: Rice production in California in 1996 is expected to rise 16 percent from 1995 levels, while production of American Pima cotton is forecast to surge by 85 percent, state officials said on Thursday.

The 1996 rice crop forecast, at 40.9 million hundredweight, is 16 percent above 1995 crop production levels. The 518,000 acres of harvest are up 11 percent from last year, according to crop estimated released by the California Department of Food and Agriculture.

Upland cotton production in California is forecast at 2.35 million bales, two percent above last year, with harvested acreage 15 percent below last year. But the yield is forecast at 1,134 pounds per acre, up 19 percent from 1995.
American Pima cotton production is forecast at 415,000 bales, up 85 percent from last year's crop. The 165,000 acres for harvest are 43 percent above last year.

California's 1996 corn for grain production is forecast at 1.08 million tons, 60 percent above last year. The forecast yield, at a record 4.90 tons per acre, is up nine percent from last year, state officials said.

The initial 1996-1997 navel orange forecast is 74 million cartons, down three percent from last season, while walnut production is forecast at 220,000 tons, down six percent from the 1995 crop of 234,000 tons, the department said.

Sugar beet production is forecast at 2.63 million tons, down 18 percent from the 1995 crop, while the initial pecan production forecast for 1996 is 2.1 million pounds, down 28 percent from last year, the department said.
